title: Ask Now, Use Later: Benchmarking the Proactivity Gap in Long-Lived LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2605.28108v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A long-lived LLM agent, such as OpenClaw, earns its value by acting on a user's preferences and constraints across sessions, not just the current request. Yet today's agents keep what a user volunteers but rarely ask for what stays unspoken, leaving a proactivity gap in long-lived LLM agents: an agent cannot act on a preference it never obtained. As users delegate more of their affairs to agents, the impact of this gap grows. We isolate one concrete, controllable slice of this gap as Ask-to-Remember (ATR): the agent decides whether to ask now for a reusable user preference that the current task does not need but a later session with the same user will. ATR is hard even to evaluate: the right question is underdetermined and its payoff deferred to tasks that may never arise. translated_title: 现在提问，之后使用：对长寿命LLM智能体中主动性缺口的基准测试
translated_abstract: 长寿命LLM智能体（如OpenClaw）的价值在于跨会话地依据用户的偏好与约束采取行动，而不仅仅是响应当前的请求。然而，如今的智能体只会保留用户主动提供的信息，却很少去询问那些未被言明的内容，这在长寿命LLM智能体中留下了一个主动性缺口：智能体无法基于它从未获得的偏好采取行动。随着用户将越来越多的事务委托给智能体，这一缺口的影响日益增大。我们从这个缺口中分离出一个具体且可控的部分，称为Ask-to-Remember（ATR，提问以记住）：即智能体决定是否现在就询问某个可复用的用户偏好——当前任务不需要它，但之后与同一用户的会话会需要。ATR甚至难以评估：正确的问题本身是不确定的，其收益要推迟到可能永远不会出现的任务中才能体现。据我们所知，ATRBench是首个ATR基准，它通过将每个用户的偏好固定为隐藏的真实标准使该问题可度量，因此成功要求……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了首个针对"提问以记住”（Ask-to-Remember）任务的基准ATRBench，用以度量和缓解长寿命LLM智能体因不主动询问用户未言明偏好而产生的主动性缺口。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ATRBench, the first benchmark for the Ask-to-Remember (ATR) task, which measures and addresses the proactivity gap in long-lived LLM agents that fail to proactively ask users about unstated preferences needed in future sessions.
